summary: Renders a GLSL shader into a TOP image with GLSL TOP behavior, but supports more than 3 input TOPs for many-texture shader pipelines. It can run vertex/pixel or compute shaders, map inputs across 3D/array slices, allocate multiple color buffers, and expose vector, CHOP-array, matrix, atomic-counter, and specialization-constant uniforms.

common_gotchas: GLSL Multi TOP follows GLSL TOP behavior but supports more than 3 inputs, so use it when input count exceeds the regular GLSL TOP input limit.
Use nonuniformEXT() when dynamically indexing sampler arrays such as sTD2DInputs[] from per-pixel shader logic.
When a compute shader reads output textures, previous output values, or feedback-style data, set Output Access to Read-Write instead of Write Only.
In N inputs per Slice mode, input mapping loops back to the first input if it runs out of inputs before the last output slice.
Use Render Select TOP to inspect color buffers beyond buffer 0 when # of Color Buffers is greater than one.
Auto Dispatch Size ensures at least one compute thread per output pixel, but custom compute shaders still need bounds guards around gl_GlobalInvocationID.
For 3D Texture or 2D Texture Array outputs, dispatch enough Z threads or use shader logic that writes all required slices.
Texture Buffer arrays hold many more CHOP array values than uniform arrays, but shader declarations must use samplerBuffer and texelFetch().
Do not include a #version statement in shader DATs because TouchDesigner adds it during compilation.
Use Info CHOP/Info DAT style diagnostics for cook, warning, error, and compile state before trusting output pixels.
